newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX chases Dow higher, rate hike fears ease.
newsitem.headline: German DAX chases Dow higher, rate hike fears ease.

text.p: German shares started Wednesday bourse trade sharply higher in a delayed reaction to a post-bourse rally on Tuesday when benign U.S. data were seen as reducing the imminent need for a U.S. interest rate rises.
German gains nonetheless failed to match the sharp 2.6 percent rise in the Dow Jones as scepticism over U.S. stock gains continued.
The DAX-30 index of leading German shares rose 64.36 points to 3,447.55 in early bourse dealings -- a gain of 1.90 percent. The June DAX future stood 24.5 points up at 3,455.5.
Dealers noted that short covering in the market, particularly on Tuesday, indicated investors thought further gains were possible but little fresh money was coming in.
Traders said the next key trading level for the DAX index was 3,475 points. Once that was breached, new inflows of money were expected.

In the short term, volumes were also thin due to Thursday's May Day holiday and ahead of further U.S. data, including the Chicago Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) later today and the non-farm payrolls report due on Friday.
Drugs group Schering gained strongly as it reported first-quarter group sales up 21 percent and promised plans for share buy-backs when German laws permitted them.
It rose 5.20 marks to 166.20 in the first half an hour of bourse trade.
Chemical and drugs giant Bayer meanwhile topped early volumes but underperformed the market after what many saw as disappointing. It could only rise seven pfennigs to 69.05.
